Body:
Closing in favour of #51129.

The right fix is to make mid-prompt completion work, not to disable the trigger. `v2` already opens the command list for a `/` token anywhere in the prompt; the list was just gated to `store.index === 0` and selecting a command cleared everything before the cursor, so the popup was empty and its `Enter` binding swallowed submission (#50604).

#51129 completes the feature on `v2`: text-expanding commands are offered mid-prompt, the selection is spliced in place, and a token that matches no command closes the popup so the prompt stays submittable. Same direction as #47450 on the v1 line.

Additional reproduction on **v2.0.16** (macOS Desktop, Apple Silicon), plus a source-level note on the gated handler.

## 1. Still broken in 2.0.16 — not just an old build

The shipped desktop bundle still contains the unconditional stub. Extracted from the running server's own web assets (`/_assets/dialog-CdLYz1aX.js`):

```js
w=M(()=>({mutationFn:async e=>{throw Error(s.t(`provider.custom.unavailable`))}, ...}))
```

No server or protocol condition. Every Submit fails with `Custom providers are unavailable on this server`, exactly as reported. So the "shipped build predates the fix" theory does not fully explain 2.0.16.

## 2. The `protocol === "v1"` gate can never pass on the bundled server

The current `dev` source gates the save on the detected server protocol:

```js
// packages/app/src/components/dialog-custom-provider.tsx
if ((await serverSDK().protocol) !== "v1") throw new Error(language.t("provider.custom.unavailable"))
```

`detectServerProtocol` (`packages/app/src/utils/server-protocol.ts`) probes `/global/health` and `/api/health` and requires a JSON body before returning `"v1"`, otherwise it defaults to `"v2"`.

On the desktop app's own bundled server (`OPENCODE_CLIENT=desktop`, v2.0.16) those probes do not return JSON:

| Probe | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /global/health` | `200` but `content-type: text/html` → HTML catch-all page, so `value` is not an object |
| `GET /api/health` | `404` → rejected by `!response.ok` |
| `GET /api/info` | `200 application/json` → works, but is not one of the probed paths |

`detectServerProtocol` therefore falls through to `return "v2"`. Combined with the `!== "v1"` check, the custom-provider dialog can never succeed on the app's own bundled v2 server — even once the save implementation actually ships. The `v1`-only gate looks like a leftover from the compatibility layer rather than an intentional product decision, since the dialog's own copy points users at the OpenAI-compatible provider docs and the equivalent manual `providers.<id>` config works fine on that same server.

## 3. Workaround (config file)

Adding the block to `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` works correctly on the bundled server, including model limits and capabilities. Verified end-to-end with `opencode run`:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "providers": {
    "myprovider": {
      "name": "My Provider",
      "env": ["MYPROVIDER_API_KEY"],
      "package": "@opencode/ai/providers/openai-compatible",
      "settings": {
        "baseURL": "http://localhost:20128/v1",
        "apiKey": "sk-..."
      },
      "models": {
        "my-model": {
          "modelID": "upstream/model-id",
          "name": "My Model",
          "limit": { "context": 200000, "output": 64000 },
          "capabilities": { "tools": true, "input": ["text", "image"], "output": ["text"] }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Suggest either shipping the save implementation without the `v1` gate, or hiding the entry point (the `dialog.provider.custom.label` entry) on v2 servers so the UI does not offer an action that cannot succeed.

## Environment

- opencode version: Desktop `2.0.16` (bundled CLI `v2.0.16`), macOS Apple Silicon (Darwin 27.0.0)
- Install/channel: release, installed via the desktop app auto-updater
- Terminal: Unavailable: Desktop (Electron) UI
- Shell: `/bin/zsh`
- Active plugins: none found in config

Follow-up on the preflight question: that failure was our setup, not this branch. Our server required a password and the client wasn't sending one. The 401 comes back with an empty body, which the client reports as "did not provide a compatible V2 health response" / `UnsupportedContentType`. `/api/health` was a red herring; the client only calls `/api/info`.

Retested `8bdbdb929` (client and `opencode serve` both built from it, on Linux):
- `/api/info` returns 401 without the password and 200 with it.
- With `OPENCODE_PASSWORD` set, the client passes the preflight, and the server records the requested launch directory as the project rather than falling back to its default.

Together with the earlier remote-only `chdir` check, the branch works end to end for us.

Separately, a 401 surfacing as an incompatible health response is misleading; that seems worth its own issue.

I had that problem too, both on Linux and Windows

Same root cause — with a data point your analysis was missing: **not all v1 sessions are affected**.

Ran the same drill on my DB (opencode 2.0.14, imported from 1.18.x):

- Of 360 imported v1 sessions, **324 survived and every single one (324/324) was a git-project session** (project id carried into the v2 `project` table, `path` already relative to the repo worktree).
- The 36 lost ones were **100% `project_id='global'` in v1 itself** (`tmp/opencode`, `home/tom/...`, media mounts) — and they were **never reassigned**: the importer's fallback at `v1-migration.bun.ts:586` only fires when the id is missing (and logs `Reassigned V1 session with missing project`), but the literal `'global'` row exists in `project` (worktree `/`), so `projects.has('global')` is `true` and the ternary keeps `'global'` verbatim. Conclusion: this is a **semantic mismatch between v1 and v2 resolution**, not the fallback branch.

Two additions beyond what's listed here:

1. **Dirs that are git today but were never tracked by v1** fall in the same lost group — v1 filed those sessions under `'global'` too. Cross-referencing the `global` rows from your query against the filesystem: some of those directories are git repos today (the repo may even post-date the sessions), yet their imported rows still carry `'global'` + a root-relative `path`. The discriminator is the v1 row's `project_id='global'`, not the current `.git` presence — V1's claim step only ran for repos it recognized.
2. A **second, independent gap**: sessions created around v1's `20260428004200_add_session_path` schema change have `path IS NULL` (90 rows in our DB, 2026-04-03→05-05). They keep the **correct** project id but are still invisible — `SessionStore.list`'s exact `eq(path, subpath)` (`packages/core/src/session/store.ts:108`) excludes `NULL` when `subpath=''`. Sister symptom to #50980, but the rows **do** exist in `session_v2`; only `path` is null.

Agree your three candidate fixes stand; my vote is the fix 1 (importer rewrite) plus the `isNull+directory` list fallback as the cheap safety net.

The underlying reason MCP child processes and Docker containers get orphaned on unexpected server termination is POSIX process hierarchy semantics. When a parent process terminates abruptly without running application-level teardown hooks, any active child processes are immediately reparented to PID 1 (or the nearest subreaper registered via `prctl(PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER, 1)`). Relying on runtime signal traps (such as Node.js `SIGTERM`/`SIGINT` handlers or Effect scope finalizers) is fundamentally non-deterministic because uncatchable signals (`SIGKILL`, Linux OOM killer invocations, or kernel panics) bypass userland run loops entirely.

On modern Linux, the deterministic OS-level primitive for child process containment is cgroups v2 combined with `cgroup.kill`. When a server or worker session initializes, its entire process tree should be placed into a dedicated cgroup leaf. When the session terminates or crashes, writing `1` to `cgroup.kill` causes the kernel to atomically deliver `SIGKILL` to every task in that cgroup simultaneously. This eliminates reparenting races, double-fork daemonization escapes, and orphaned background containers.

For child processes directly spawned via `fork()`/`execve()`, setting `prctl(PR_SET_PDEATHSIG, SIGTERM)` between fork and exec guarantees that the immediate child receives a termination signal if the parent dies, though it does not automatically protect against grandchildren that invoke `setsid()`. Combining `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` with PID namespaces (`CLONE_NEWPID`) provides complete lifecycle binding: when the namespace init process exits, the kernel destroys all remaining tasks inside that namespace.

Disclaimer: I am the author/maintainer of [Vetto](https://github.com/shleder/vetto), an open-source sandbox runtime for AI coding agents. We addressed this exact failure mode for agent MCP servers and sub-processes by wrapping executions in ephemeral cgroups v2 scopes with automated `cgroup.kill` teardown and PID tracking via `pidfd_open`/`pidfd_send_signal`, guaranteeing zero orphaned child processes on exit without requiring external supervisor daemons.

Blocking `require`, `import()`, and `process` at the JavaScript interpreter level is insufficient to enforce a true security boundary. Standard HTTP client implementations (such as `undici` in Node.js, native fetch in Bun/Deno, or Chromium network stacks) implement URL resolution in native C++ runtime bindings. When a model executes `fetch('file:///etc/hosts')`, the file access occurs via low-level native `openat()` syscalls that bypass JavaScript-level property proxying or module loaders entirely.

To prevent unauthorized filesystem and local host access, the boundary must be enforced by the Linux kernel:

1. **Filesystem Boundary via Landlock LSM**: Rather than intercepting module imports in userland, Landlock LSM (ABI 1–6) allows an unprivileged process to restrict its own filesystem access rules. Applying a Landlock ruleset before executing untrusted agent code restricts `openat()`, `read()`, and directory traversal at the kernel VFS layer. Any native attempt by `fetch()` to open `file:///etc/hosts` or credentials like `~/.ssh` fails immediately with `EACCES`.
2. **Network Boundary via Network Namespaces**: Moving untrusted code into a dedicated unprivileged network namespace (`CLONE_NEWNET`) with only a loopback interface guarantees that outbound network requests cannot reach the host network stack, cloud metadata endpoints (`169.254.169.254`), or internal microservices. When external model communication is required, requests should pass through an explicit Unix domain socket or L7 proxy with TLS ClientHello SNI inspection.

Disclaimer: I am the author/maintainer of [Vetto](https://github.com/shleder/vetto), an open-source security runtime for AI coding tools. Vetto executes agent commands inside unprivileged Linux user/mount/network namespaces with automatic Landlock LSM policy compilation and tmpfs secret masking, blocking host and file probes with sub-4ms cold start latency without needing Docker.

_The following comment was made by an LLM, it may be inaccurate:_

Both errors come from AgentRouter-side checks:
- `401 unauthorized client detected`: AgentRouter only accepts supported clients. OpenCode is supported when set up as in https://agentrouter.org/docs/opencode.html (`@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`, baseURL `https://agentrouter.org/v1`). Raw curl or custom apps get this 401 even with a valid key.
- `400 content blocked`: per their FAQ, only Chinese, English, French, German and Russian prompts are allowed.

Adding a related symptom from the HTTP API side. I verified it on 2.0.15 (Windows 11). The same code is unchanged in v2.0.16 and on the current `v2` tip (`19a9e41c28`).

With persistence off, the live half of `follow=true` on the session log is empty too, not only the replay. A follower gets the `log.synced` marker and then nothing. The same mutations appear on `/api/event` immediately:

```
[   27 ms] follow: log.synced seq=0
[ 1447 ms] PATCH title=renamed 1 -> 204
[ 1972 ms] instance event stream: session.renamed
[ 2968 ms] PATCH title=renamed 2 -> 204
[ 2976 ms] instance event stream: session.renamed
[ 7541 ms] replay (follow=false): data: {"type":"log.synced","aggregateID":"ses_…","seq":2}
```

The aggregate sequence advances to 2, but no durable event reaches the follower.

As far as I can tell, this happens because the live tail is a wake-up followed by a re-read of `EventTable`. The committed event itself is never pushed:

**Landru is thinking on behalf of Jeff:** (Follow-up from the same agent that filed this; verified against current `origin/v2` at `a16eedfe`.)

Two updates from porting work since this was filed:

**1. The publish route is not just missing - it was removed outright.** The v1 server exposed `POST /tui/publish` (that was `client.tui.publish`'s transport). The v2 server package (`packages/server/src/`) now contains zero references to TUI events - no route, no handler. The `TuiEvent` schema (`packages/schema/src/tui-event.ts`) survives, and the TUI still consumes it, but nothing server-side can produce those events anymore.

**2. The more useful ask is probably tab-scoped, not app-scoped.** v2's multi-tab model changes what "exit" should mean for a plugin. The TUI registry now has both:

- `app.exit` ("Exit the application") - on a shared daemon this takes down every tab.
- `session.tab.close` ("Close current session tab", `app.tsx:824`, keybind `<leader>w`) - ends the current session's tab and leaves the rest running.

Our plugin's exit command runs a persistence checklist and then ends the session it belongs to. On v2 the right target is `session.tab.close`, not `app.exit` - closing the whole daemon from one session's slash command would be wrong when other tabs are open. The `tui.command.execute` schema's command field is an open union (`Schema.Literals([...]) | Schema.String`), so `session.tab.close` is already a legal payload; the only missing piece is still the publish path.

So the refined ask: when a publish surface returns, make sure the tab-scoped lifecycle commands (`session.tab.close` in particular) are reachable from server-side plugins, not just the app-level ones. For our case that would make the plugin's exit command do the right thing on a multi-tab host: close its own tab, flush everything, and leave the daemon and other sessions alone.
